title: Non-Coprime CRT: Image Characterization
description: Formalizes the generalized Chinese Remainder Theorem for non-coprime moduli: characterizes when the system x ≡ a (mod m), x ≡ b (mod n) is solvable (iff gcd(m,n) | (a-b)), proves uniqueness modulo lcm(m,n), and gives an explicit solution formula via Bézout coefficients.

overview.historicalContext:
**Non-Coprime Chinese Remainder Theorem**

The standard CRT requires gcd(m,n) = 1. When moduli are not coprime, the natural map ℤ → ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ is no longer surjective. The generalized CRT characterizes exactly which pairs (a,b) lie in the image: precisely those satisfying a ≡ b (mod gcd(m,n)). Solutions, when they exist, are unique modulo lcm(m,n) rather than mod mn. This extends the classical CRT to handle arbitrary moduli.
overview.problemStatement: **Theorem**: The system x ≡ a (mod m), x ≡ b (mod n) has a solution if and only if gcd(m,n) | (a - b). When solutions exist, they are unique modulo lcm(m,n), and an explicit solution is given by x = a - m · gcdA(m,n) · ((a-b)/gcd(m,n)).
overview.proofStrategy:
The proof proceeds in six parts:

1. **Forward direction**: If x solves both congruences, then m | (a-x) and n | (b-x), so gcd(m,n) divides both, hence gcd(m,n) | (a-b).
2. **Backward direction**: Given gcd(m,n) | (a-b), use Bézout coefficients to construct x = a - m · gcdA · k where k = (a-b)/gcd. The key identity is proved by `linear_combination`.
3. **Uniqueness**: If x,y both solve the system, then m | (x-y) and n | (x-y), so lcm(m,n) | (x-y) via `Nat.lcm_dvd`.
4. **Explicit formula**: `genCRTSolution` packages the construction with verified congruences.
5. **Special cases**: Coprime case recovers standard CRT; concrete examples demonstrate solvable and unsolvable instances.
6. **Full theorem**: Combines existence and uniqueness into a single statement.
keyInsights: The solvability condition gcd(m,n) | (a-b) is both necessary and sufficient — a complete characterization
Solutions are unique mod lcm(m,n), not mod mn — reflecting that the map ℤ → ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ has kernel lcm(m,n)ℤ
Bézout coefficients (gcdA, gcdB) provide the explicit construction, with `linear_combination` handling the algebraic verification
The coprime case (gcd = 1) recovers standard CRT since 1 divides everything and lcm(m,n) = mn
Going through natAbs for the lcm uniqueness proof bridges Nat.lcm and Int divisibility cleanly

sections.title: Solvability Condition
sections.summary: Proves both directions: the system x ≡ a (mod m), x ≡ b (mod n) is solvable iff gcd(m,n) | (a-b). Forward: transitivity of divisibility. Backward: Bézout coefficient construction.

sections.title: Uniqueness Modulo LCM
sections.summary: Two solutions to the same system are congruent mod lcm(m,n). Uses natAbs bridge to apply Nat.lcm_dvd, then case-splits on sign.

sections.title: GCD-LCM Relationship
sections.summary: The fundamental identity m*n = gcd(m,n) * lcm(m,n) and the coprime specialization lcm(m,n) = mn.

sections.title: Explicit Solution Formula
sections.summary: Defines genCRTSolution and verifies it satisfies both congruences. The second congruence proof uses linear_combination with the Bézout equation.

sections.title: Special Cases and Examples
sections.summary: Coprime case recovers standard CRT. Concrete examples: (4,6) solvable with gcd=2, (4,6) unsolvable when 2 does not divide, (6,9) solvable with gcd=3.

sections.title: Complete Characterization
sections.summary: Reformulates solvability as a modular congruence a ≡ b (mod gcd(m,n)). Combines existence and uniqueness into the full generalized CRT theorem.

conclusion.summary: This formalization fully proves the generalized Chinese Remainder Theorem for non-coprime moduli with 0 sorries and 0 axioms. It provides: (1) a complete solvability characterization, (2) uniqueness modulo lcm, (3) an explicit computable solution formula, and (4) concrete examples demonstrating both solvable and unsolvable systems.
conclusion.implications:
**Mathematical Significance**

1. **Completeness**: Unlike the standard CRT which requires coprimality, this handles arbitrary moduli and characterizes exactly when solutions exist.
2. **Constructivity**: The explicit formula via Bézout coefficients is algorithmically computable, giving an effective solution method.
3. **Structural insight**: The image of ℤ → ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ is characterized by the congruence condition modulo gcd, revealing the kernel-cokernel structure.
4. **Foundation for extensions**: This result generalizes to k-fold non-coprime systems and to general Dedekind domains.
openQuestions: Can this be extended to systems of k simultaneous congruences with arbitrary (non-pairwise-coprime) moduli?
Can the image of the map ℤ/mnℤ → ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ be characterized as a subring, and its index computed?
Can the non-coprime CRT be formalized for general PIDs or Dedekind domains?
